editorial:
Imagine being a teenage genius who just wants to set the world on fire with your words. You get to follow Arthur Rimbaud from his moody school days in France all the way to his lonely old age in Africa. The movie feels like a long journey through the life of a man who could never quite fit in. It captures that feeling of being young, angry, and desperate to create something new. You will see him struggle with his family and his wild relationship with another poet, making the whole story feel personal and raw rather than like a boring history lesson.

The acting is top-notch, and the way the movie jumps through time keeps you interested. While some parts move a bit slow, the beautiful scenery makes up for it. If you like stories about rebels and artists, you will love this. To get the best experience, you should definitely stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video to see all the detail in the landscapes. If you are a movie collector, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is a great call because the colors are just stunning.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, you see an older Rimbaud living in Africa, far away from the fame of his early poems. He has completely given up writing to trade goods and live a quiet life. He refuses to let people publish his old work, showing that he finally found peace in silence. The movie ends with him looking at the ocean, knowing he lived a full life on his own terms.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves stories about misunderstood geniuses and historical dramas.
